1	# Agent definition
2	
3	## Why
4	
5	Blind planning exists because a planner that can read the code inherits the code's mistakes as constraints. Every workaround becomes an implicit requirement, and the feature gets shaped to fit the defect. Deriving the spec from intent alone makes disagreement between intent and implementation visible rather than silently absorbed. Phase 2 is not "soften the spec until it fits"; it is "name each disagreement and rule on it", with the code as the presumed-wrong party.
6	
7	## Engines
8	
9	A session runs on one engine, chosen per session or per phase:
10	
11	- Claude through the Agent SDK (Claude Code as a library, JavaScript build, inherited Claude Code login).
12	- GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi K3 through Berget AI (OpenAI-compatible) with our own loop and tools.
13	
14	The extension only sees `CodeSession`: send a prompt, stream events, answer permission requests, interrupt. Engines differ below that line.
15	
16	## Shape
17	
18	Three phases, each a separate session with its own system prompt and tool set. Handoff is files on disk, never conversation context.
19	
20	```
21	docs/intent/**  +  work item  →  spec.md  →  plan.md  →  code
22	                    (blind)      (reconcile)   (implement)
23	```
24	
25	## Phase 1: Blind plan
26	
27	Sees: feature description, domain brief (ubiquitous language, stack, constraints), `docs/intent/**`, one work item closure when ADO is connected.
28	Never sees: source, descriptive docs, PRs, build output.
29	
30	Until ADO is connected the feature description is typed by the user or picked from `docs/intent/**`. The agent plans the user story itself; the spec's task list is the source for the ADO tasks created under the story once ADO is connected (write-back, not read-only).
31	
32	Tools: Read/Glob scoped to `docs/intent/**`, `get_work_item(id)`, AskUserQuestion, optionally WebSearch. Bash denied by bare name (allow-lists only auto-approve; a bare-name deny removes the tool from context).
33	
34	First a direction in chat (the decisions that shape the feature, the questions that would change them); nothing is written until the user says go. Then `plan/<feature>.spec.md`: goal and behaviour always, edge cases, tasks and open questions when the feature has them, stable item IDs. To the point, not complete: an item earns its place by changing what gets built or how it is tested. No file paths. If `docs/intent/**` has nothing on the feature, ask and stop.
35	
36	### get_work_item
37	
38	Hand-coded, read-only, Azure DevOps. Server-side filtering is the enforcement.
39	
40	- Include: title, description, parent chain, Goal/Actor/Impact/Behaviour/Example.
41	- Exclude: state, comments, tasks, linked PRs/commits/branches/builds, `System.*` and `Microsoft.VSTS.*` fields.
42	- Walks parents, children, related. Depth and total caps, cycle detection, deterministic ordering. Returns markdown. Snapshot to `plan/<feature>.context.md`.
43	- State is excluded deliberately: a Done item over drifted code is evidence for phase 2, not input to phase 1.
44	- Prose may leak file paths; accepted, or stripped in the tool.
45	
46	### Docs split
47	
48	`docs/intent/**` is phase 1 scope. Everything else is phase 2 only. Descriptive docs drift with the code in the same direction and arrive labelled as authority.
49	
50	## Phase 2: Reconcile
51	
52	Tools: Read, Glob, Grep. Edit/Write/Bash denied by bare name.
53	Input: spec + context + repo. Not the phase 1 transcript.
54	
55	Output `plan/<feature>.plan.md`, front-matter `status: draft|approved`, one verdict per spec item:
56	
57	| verdict | meaning |
58	|---|---|
59	| matches | nothing to do |
60	| drifted | correct the code |
61	| naive | amend spec, reason required |
62	| conflict | sources disagree, human decides |
63	
64	Authority order is fixed in the prompt: work item, then intent doc, then code. Amendments (`naive`) and drift findings are written back to `docs/intent/**` or the work item as an explicit output, so intent does not rot.
65	
66	## Retrieval
67	
68	A sub-session the planner calls with `retrieve(question, known, budget)` to keep file dumps out of its own context. Phase 2 first; phase 1 only when the intent tree or work-item graph outgrows the planner.
69	
70	- Locates and quotes, never interprets. Output is verbatim excerpts with provenance; the planner rules on them. A summary drops nuance silently, and the planner never sees what was left out.
71	- Tools are derived, not configured: the calling phase's tool set minus AskUserQuestion and anything that writes. Phase 1 retrieval is blind by construction.
72	- No user interaction, no recursion. "Needs X to answer" goes in `not_found`; the planner decides whether to ask. Depth 1.
73	- Result: `findings[]` (excerpt, source as `path#heading`, work item id or URL, one line on why it matches), `not_found[]` (what was looked for, where), `status: complete | partial | budget_exhausted`. Partial is a result, not an error.
74	- Written to `.agent/runs/<id>/retrieval/<n>.md`; the tool returns path, status and counts. Files on disk, not conversation context.
75	- Budget per call (tool calls, tokens), set by the planner. Exhaustion returns findings so far.
76	- Runs as a `CodeSession` under its own profile; a cheap model is fine because the task is search.
77	- Independent questions fan out as independent sessions, no shared state.
78	
79	## Phase 3: Implement
80	
81	Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, task state. Input is the approved plan file only, fresh session; refuses to start on `status: draft`. Drift items are work items alongside feature items.
82	
83	- Verification hook after edits: build scoped to the project owning the edited file, test selection, run on plan-item boundary; failure budget of N consecutive failed fixes per item, then stop and write the failure into the plan.
84	- Read-before-edit staleness: refuse to edit an unread file, re-read when changed underneath.
85	- Explicit task state so item 4 of 7 does not vanish.
86	- Done when the acceptance-criteria tests pass, not when the model stops.
87	
88	## Instructions
89	
90	Small shared core plus a per-phase file. Per-type rules inject via PreToolUse hook matched on the path at edit time.
91	
92	- Checkable rules (no `#region`, no AutoMapper/MediatR, nullable on, no `Any`) go to analyzers, `.editorconfig`, BannedApiAnalyzers, grep in the verification hook.
93	- Judgment rules (rule of three, earned abstraction) go to the prompt.
94	- A phase file over a page means the excess is checkable or is spec. Remove alternatives instead of instructing tool preference.
95	
96	## Coordination
97	
98	Claim registry `.agent/sessions/<id>.json`: claimed files, `plan_item_id`, `deadline` set by the session, heartbeat. PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write claims on first touch, denies if another live session holds the file and names who.
99	
100	- Session reports completion and releases the claim. Silence past `deadline` is the stale signal.
101	- Stale claims are flagged in the UI, never auto-released.
102	- Force-release posts a revocation message into the session. The session stops immediately, does not finish the in-flight edit, reports touched files.
103	
104	Checkpoints, opt-in: `checkpoint(reason)` scoped to files under the session's claims; `revert` hash-compares and refuses files that moved underneath. No git. Repeated checkpoints on one plan item mean the item was underspecified; log the reasons.
105	
106	Channels, non-blocking: `send(session, text)` returns immediately; notification is a one-line tail on the receiver's next tool result; `read_messages()` pulls the payload. Registry before channels. Cap thread length and escalate to the user.
107	
108	## Observability
109	
110	Run id, per-phase transcript, tool calls, token spend, checkpoint reasons under `.agent/runs/<id>/`.
111	
112	## Per-phase model
113	
114	Phase 1 wants the strongest reasoner, phase 3 wants throughput. Profiles carry engine, model and effort.
115	
116	## Parked
117	
118	- ADO: `get_work_item` and creating tasks under the user story from the spec's task list. No work items exist yet.
119	- Repo map for phases 2 and 3 (project list, public type index, folder conventions).
120	- Anthropic Messages API adapter under API key in the own-loop engine.
121	- Compaction in the own-loop engine.
122	- Retrieval in phase 1 (large intent tree, work-item graph, WebSearch).
123

event.text:
I read `docs/intent/agent.md` and the feature docs. There is no feature doc for this one, but the surrounding intent is clear enough to derive a direction: both planning phases end in a file with stable item ids and a `status: draft|approved` gate, and the plan bar today offers only Open and Approve. Commenting is the missing middle — the way a human says "not this" without hand-editing the artifact.

**What it is**

- A review pass over a draft plan artifact: the human attaches notes to individual items by their stable id (B2, T3, a reconcile verdict row) and to the plan as a whole, and can strike a proposed item.
- Comments are collected and submitted as one batch, not one message per note. A plan review is several remarks at once, and each submission costs a turn.
- The agent revises the artifact and answers every comment: addressed, or disagreed with a reason. Disagreement is allowed but visible — the same spirit as reconcile's `naive` verdict, where the spec can be wrong but never silently.
- A plan with unresolved comments cannot be approved. That is the point of the gate.

**Where it could go two ways**

1. *Which artifact.* I propose one mechanism over any draft plan artifact — phase-1 spec and phase-2 plan alike. Both have stable ids and the same approve gate; two review mechanisms would be one too many. Commenting an *approved* plan mid-implementation is out of scope.
2. *Is a strike binding?* I propose binding: the item is marked removed, never renumbered (the id stays, so later discussion still resolves), and the agent may not resurrect it — but the agent does the rewriting, so items that depended on it get repaired. A strike the agent can argue away makes the gesture worthless; a strike applied mechanically leaves dangling references.
3. *Who revises.* I propose: the owning session if it is still alive, otherwise a fresh session of the same phase reading artifact + comments from disk. Handoff is files, never transcript — so a reload must not lose the ability to revise.
4. *Anchoring.* Item ids only, plus one plan-level comment. No line- or word-level anchors on arbitrary prose: ids are the plan's own addressing scheme, and prose gets rewritten out from under an anchor.
5. *Persistence.* Comments and their resolutions survive reload and stay readable after approval, so the review is part of the record — not a chat message that scrolls away.

**What it is not:** threaded discussion, comments on code or diffs, a replacement for hand-editing the file in the editor, and not a way to add new items by comment — a comment can ask for one, the agent writes it.

**Questions that would change the above**

- Q: Should a comment be able to *edit the text* of an item directly (human types the replacement wording), or only describe what is wrong? I assumed describe-only; direct edit makes the agent's coherence pass ambiguous.
- Q: After revision, does the plan return to the human automatically for another round, or does the agent re-run its own checks first? I assumed it returns immediately — `needs_human`.
- Q: Does striking the last item of a plan, or striking so much that the goal no longer holds, need special handling, or is that just the human's problem?

Say go and I will write the spec.
the revised plan should be shown to the human.

---
feature: commenting a plan
status: draft
---

# commenting a plan

## Goal
A human reviewing a draft plan artifact — a blind-plan spec or a reconcile plan — needs a way to say "this item is wrong" and "drop this one" without hand-editing the file and without approving something they disagree with. Today the only gestures are Open and Approve, so a plan that is nearly right has to be argued for in free chat and re-derived from memory. Commenting gives the review a shape: notes attached to the plan's own item ids, strikes on items that should not be built, one submission back to the agent, a revised plan shown to the human, and an answer to every comment. Approval stays blocked until the review is closed, so agreement is reached rather than assumed.

## Behaviour
- B1: While a plan artifact's status is draft, the human can attach a free-text comment to any item by its stable id, and one comment to the plan as a whole. Ids are the only anchor; there is no line- or word-level anchoring.
- B2: The human can strike a proposed item, and unstrike it, for as long as the review is unsubmitted.
- B3: Comments and strikes accumulate as a pending review, visible as a whole before it is sent, and submitted in one batch.
- B4: Submitting hands the artifact and the review to the session that owns the artifact if it is still alive, and otherwise to a fresh session of the same phase that reads both from disk. No part of the review depends on the transcript.
- B5: On revision, every struck item is marked removed in the artifact. Ids are never renumbered or reused, and items that referred to a removed item are repaired so the plan stays coherent.
- B6: Every comment in the review gets a resolution from the agent: addressed, or disagreed with a stated reason. A comment is never dropped without a resolution.
- B7: After revising, the agent presents the revised plan to the human — what changed since the review was submitted, and each comment with its resolution — and the session goes to `needs_human`. The human may open another review round on the revised plan.
- B8: The human closes a comment by accepting its resolution, or leaves it open by commenting again in the next round. Accepting a disagreement is an explicit act.
- B9: A struck item stays removed. The agent may not reintroduce it in this or a later round; only a new comment from the human can bring it back.
- B10: A plan artifact cannot be approved while any comment is open.
- B11: Comments, strikes and resolutions survive a reload and remain readable after approval, as part of the record of how the plan was reached.
- B12: Commenting is offered only on a draft artifact. An approved plan is not commentable; it is reopened or superseded.

## Edge cases
- E1: The human comments on an item already marked removed → allowed, and it is the way to ask for a struck item back; the reversal is the human's decision, not the agent's (B9).
- E2: A review is submitted with no comments and no strikes → rejected as empty; no turn is spent.
- E3: Every item in the plan is struck → the agent reports that nothing remains rather than inventing a replacement plan; the human restates the feature or abandons it.
- E4: The agent disagrees with all comments and changes nothing → the plan is still presented to the human with its resolutions (B7), and approval stays blocked until each comment is closed (B8, B10).
- E5: A comment's id is no longer present in the artifact, because the file was edited by hand → the comment is kept and given to the agent together with the item text it was written against, never silently discarded.

## Tasks
- T1: Review authoring — attach, edit and remove comments per item id and for the plan as a whole; strike and unstrike; show the pending review as a whole; persist it across reloads; offer it only on a draft (B1, B2, B3, B11, B12, E2).
- T2: Submission and handoff — route the artifact plus review to the owning or a fresh same-phase session, reading from disk rather than transcript, carrying orphaned comments with their original item text (B4, E5).
- T3: Revision conduct — the agent marks struck items removed without renumbering, repairs dependents, resolves every comment as addressed or disagreed with reason, never resurrects a struck item, and reports an emptied plan (B5, B6, B9, E3).
- T4: Round closure — present the revised plan with changes and resolutions, return to `needs_human`, let the human accept a resolution or comment again, and block approval while a comment is open (B7, B8, B10, E1, E4).

## Open questions
- Q1: May a comment carry replacement wording for an item, or only describe what is wrong? The spec assumes describe-only, so the agent owns every word in the artifact.
- Q2: Should review rounds be part of what is written back to a work item once ADO is connected, or stay local to the workspace? Assumed local for now.

The spec follows the direction you steered, with your correction folded in: after revising, the agent presents the revised plan back to the human with a summary of what changed and a resolution per comment (B7), and the human can open another round.
